objectives: This course provides essential Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) knowledge. In addition to maximize shareholder value, we discuss how firms involve CSR activities to maximize stakeholder value. Specifically, you are expected to know (i) What drives corporate social responsibility? (ii) How does the top management team affect CSR? (iii) How does CSR reshape corporate investment decisions and financing decisions? (iv) Do firms with more CSR activities better weather negative shocks? (v) CSR and supply chain management, (vi) Does climate change have any real effect on firms? If yes, what can we do to mitigate the negative impact? and (vii) corporate governance in the world.
content:
“Introduction of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)
CSR: Legal origin, politics, and family environment
CSR: Career concern and institutional investor
CSR and investment decisions
CSR: Capital structure, cost of debt, corporate liquidity management
CSR and supply chain management
CSR: Product market behavior, covid-19 and others
Corporate governance: General/Survey
Corporate governance: Compensation
Corporate governance: Ownership structure
Corporate governance: Board structure
Corporate governance: Law and finance“
books: “Academic journal articles from American Economic Review, Quarterly Journal of Economics, Journal of Political Economy, Journal of Finance, Journal of Financial Economics, Review of Financial Studies, Journal of Corporate Finance, Strategic Management Journal, Management Science, and so on.“
